sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Saudi National Charged with Spying on OpenAI
cards.content: A Saudi national, Abdulrahman Alfozan, has been accused of having support from the Saudi government and charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms. Alfozan, an engineer, worked for the AI firm for about a year before his alleged attempt. US prosecutors claim he was in frequent communication with a member of the Saudi royal family and had a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia booked for his wife and son. The court denied Alfozan's request for bail, citing a risk of non-appearance, and he is scheduled to appear in federal court in San Francisco. If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

cards.title: Vinted removes suspected looting listings after French riots
cards.content: Second-hand re-selling platform Vinted removed listings believed to be from looted French shops after weekend riots. The company took immediate action to identify and remove the listings, stating zero tolerance for the sale of stolen goods. Over 2,000 businesses were impacted by the violence, resulting in hundreds of millions of euros in damage. Vinted is working with French authorities and police to detect and counter emerging risks and malicious behavior.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Astronomers Map WASP-17b's Weather Using James Webb Space Telescope
cards.content: Astronomers have successfully mapped the weather patterns on a distant planet, WASP-17b, using the James Webb Space Telescope. The planet, a hot Jupiter, has one side that extends farther into space than the other, creating an uneven outline. The team, led by Cornell University and the University of Bristol, used a method called transmission strings to analyze the light passing through different parts of the atmosphere's edge. This allowed them to distinguish conditions around the boundary and create a comprehensive three-dimensional view of the planet's atmosphere. The findings agree with theoretical predictions and provide a benchmark for comparison with other exoplanets. The successful demonstration opens the way to applying this method to many more planets, potentially revealing complex weather patterns in exoplanet climates.

cards.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover to Examine Mysterious Martian Rock Layer
cards.content: NASA's Curiosity rover is on its way to examine a Martian rock layer that appears out of place and may have formed from ancient volcanic ash. The layer, known as a yardang, stretches 10 miles across the northwestern reaches of Mount Sharp on Mars. Mission scientists are excited to study the layer closely, as it could provide clues about Mars' history. The rover has been climbing Mount Sharp since 2014, and its ascent has been marked by the discovery of different geological formations, including spiderweb-like boxwork ridges. The rover is now in the second year of its fifth extended mission, during which it will drive through layers enriched with sulfates and carbonates, signs of ancient drying at the surface. Scientists expect increasingly detailed images as the rover approaches the yardangs, with the goal of reaching the base of the cliffs by 2027 to collect data and investigate how they formed.

cards.title: AI replaces switchboard jobs, shifting women's roles
cards.content: Before Siri and Alexa, there were women operating switchboards, a vital job that dominated the lives of many white, US-born women under 20. Today, this job is gone, and the dawn of artificial intelligence raises concerns about the impact on society, culture, and the economy. Women are likely to be affected by AI, which focuses on routine tasks and numbers, similar to the clerical jobs that many women hold. Historically, technological progress has led to changes in the job market, and women have adapted, moving into new roles as the economy evolves. With AI, there is a potential outcome where it eliminates tasks but not entire jobs, allowing workers to focus on higher-value tasks. However, the future is uncertain, as AI can learn and adapt.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Type 2 Diabetes Patients With Stable Rhythms Control Blood Sugar Better
cards.content: Patients with type 2 diabetes who use insulin have a better chance of controlling their blood sugar levels if they have a consistent daily rhythm. Researchers found that patients with the most stable daily rhythms were 2.3 times more likely to meet their blood sugar goals compared to those with less stable rhythms. The study, which involved 122 patients, also found that patients who were more active in the afternoon had smaller swings in their blood sugar levels. Additionally, patients who got sufficient sleep had a lower risk of having low blood sugar and smaller glucose fluctuations. The researchers believe that maintaining regular daily rhythms can help manage blood sugar levels and plan to conduct a follow-up study to confirm this.

cards.title: Scientists Study 'Immortal Jellyfish' Rejuvenation Secrets
cards.content: Scientists have discovered a unique property of the Turritopsis dohrnii jellyfish, also known as the 'immortal jellyfish', which can rewind its life cycle and revert to a younger state. This process involves a transformation of adult cells into stem cells, allowing the jellyfish to create a new polyp and eventually grow into adult jellyfish again. Researchers are studying the genetic and molecular processes behind this phenomenon, hoping to unlock its secrets and potentially apply them to human cells to treat age-related diseases. While the goal is not to reverse human aging entirely, scientists aim to explore ways to coax human cells into more youthful states to heal wounds and treat age-related maladies. The research is still in its early stages, but initial findings suggest that the immortal jellyfish's ability to rejuvenate may be linked to its enhanced ability to repair DNA damage and maintain telomeres, which could hold the key to understanding and potentially applying its regenerative abilities to humans.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Antarctic ice cliffs stabilizing, challenging climate projections
cards.content: A recent study using satellite data from NASA's Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) has found that Antarctic ice cliffs, previously thought to be unstable and prone to rapid collapse, are actually stabilizing over time. The four-year survey of over 15,000 ice cliffs found that the tallest cliffs did collapse, but the ice sheet retreated faster than predicted and then stabilized. The researchers analyzed the data and found that factors such as the shape of the land beneath the ice, the thickness of the ice, and the surrounding water level all play a role in stabilizing the cliffs. This challenges previous assumptions about runaway ice loss and its contribution to rising sea levels. The study's findings suggest that the impact of climate change on sea levels may be less severe than previously thought.

cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals. Rising temperatures and shifting weather patterns are disrupting the seasonal migrations and livelihoods of pastoral-nomadic communities

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Harryhausen's Monster Figures on Display in Winchester
cards.content: An exhibition showcasing the original monster figures and artwork of special effects pioneer Ray Harryhausen is now on display at The Arc in Winchester, Hampshire. The exhibit features models from Harryhausen's classic films, including Jason and the Argonauts, The Golden Voyage of Sinbad, One Million Years B.C., and Clash of the Titans. Harryhausen's daughter, Vanessa, remembers her childhood home being filled with the models, which her father used to create stop-motion animations. The exhibit also highlights Harryhausen's painstaking process of creating dynamic sequences by moving each model a fraction at a time. The collection is in remarkable condition, thanks to instructions left by Harryhausen, and is expected to inspire new generations to appreciate his work.

cards.title: Paul Shipper: From Film Fan to Illustrator of Marvel and Star Wars
cards.content: Paul Shipper, a film fan-turned-illustrator, has come a long way from creating movie poster artwork for fun. He has worked on some of Hollywood's biggest franchises, including Marvel, Indiana Jones, and Star Wars. Shipper's passion for illustration started when he was a kid, inspired by the films of George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He shared his designs online, which led to opportunities that once seemed like a dream. The illustrator has worked on various projects, including posters and artwork for blockbuster titles, and has maintained a consistent artistic style despite working across different projects. Shipper is now involved in a charity exhibition, AMPjam Presents: We've Been Framed, which brings together more than 60 artists from around the world to create original artworks inspired by films and television shows.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Private companies profit from taxpayer-funded housing
cards.content: Private companies are making huge profits by receiving housing benefits for vulnerable people, including those with additional needs, but failing to provide required support. These companies are exploiting the system, using social media to lure people into taxpayer-funded housing with promises of free rooms and other perks. The system, called supported exempt accommodation (SEA), is designed to provide housing and care, but charities, politicians, and residents report that many parts of the system are being exploited, with most welfare payments being made to non-profit registered providers who then hire private companies to manage properties. In Birmingham alone, the Department for Work and Pensions paid out £410m in the last financial year, and critics say that some housing providers are making a profit while providing poor support.

cards.title: UK Home Sellers Cut Prices by £21,000 Amid Mortgage Rate Surge
cards.content: In Britain, home sellers reduced asking prices on over 3,000 properties daily in September, the highest monthly total in 15 years, according to Rightmove. The surge in properties on the market, combined with some sellers setting unrealistic expectations, drove the price cuts. With mortgage rates at a three-year high, buyers are being cautious and selective, with many working to a tight budget. The average price reduction was nearly 7%, equivalent to £21,000 cut from a typical home. Properties with price reductions typically took 119 days to sell, compared to 39 days for those listed at one price. Buyers are in the driving seat, and sellers are facing difficulties, particularly those selling leasehold properties in England.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
